name: Trezco
backstory: Comes from a line of Terfila sailors who claim an ancestor helped raise the first stones of the crossing temple, long before Gorff's masons patched a single roof tile.

experience.text: Heard that Farlo and Tamuken now have a child, Farmuken.
Had a child with Forliamus, named Forliazco.
Had a child with Tamuken, named Tamuzco.
Heard that Forliamus and Farlo now have a child, Forliarlo.
Heard that Tamuken and Forliazco now have a child, Forliuken.
Heard that Forliazco and Farlo now have a child, Farliazco.
Heard that Forliazco and Farmuken now have a child, Forliamuk.
Had a child with Farlo, named Trezarlo.

criterion.standard: counts keeping the sailors' side of the temple's story alive above staying quiet about it
criterion.wasted_life: letting his own family's claim on the temple's first stones go unspoken
criterion.derivation: collision between his backstory (family claims to have helped raise the temple) and temple_of_the_crossing itself
criterion.trusts: a story that's been carried and retold and still holds together
criterion.distrusts: a record that insists on a precision no one who was actually there ever needed

routines.routine_actions: walks the transit route between Terfila and the crossing whenever a ship's in port too long to be worth waiting on, always finds a reason to pass by the temple on the way

arc.premise: With the crossing temple already granting that his family's ancestor helped raise it, Trezco wants an actual marker cut and set into the temple's own stone - a mason willing to do the work and a plain word that it's earned, not just a line in some ledger no visitor ever reads.
